clue.text: 'Hip!', Alma tells powerful connections

parts.note: with the punctuation ignored these letters show two words for chums sitting inside a word for raised ground

explanation.surface: Alma cheers somebody on, and the clue pretends that is how you make useful contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the punctuation: HIPALMATELLS is HI(PAL MATE)LLS, pals and mates inside the hills, a picture of the answer read as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for influential acquaintances who can pull strings, which is what powerful connections are.

clue.text: 'With body to die for', agreed about divine creature

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, so this says the inside of the word for is lost
about signals turning the word round, here the synonym for agreed

parts.note: aye is a way of saying yes, so agreed

explanation.surface: Someone quotes the phrase 'a body to die for' and agrees about a heavenly being's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With body to die' means the middle of a word is lost; 'about' turns the synonym of 'agreed' round.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and beauty, so she is a divine being.

clue.text: Bad good? One senior officer's admitting this doesn't make sense

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the officer's letters take others inside

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether bad can be good, with an officer taking in an argument that doesn't hold together.
explanation.walkthrough: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding; it takes in G and I to give OGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogic is reasoning that fails to hang together, the quality of not making sense.

clue.text: End of comedian's only funny material

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the comedian's name
funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A stand-up's only funny material, as a critic might grudgingly say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' gives N, the final letter of comedian; 'funny' shuffles N with ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a kind of material for clothing.

clue.text: Crosses line out in Juvenal's work

indicators.note: out tells us to remove the abbreviation for line from the crosses

parts.note: saltires are diagonal crosses in heraldry, as on the Scottish flag

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a line out while editing the work of a Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' looks like a verb but is the noun SALTIRES (X-shaped crosses), and 'out' removes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was a Roman poet famous for his sixteen satires mocking the vices of Rome.

clue.text: A minor skin problem

parts.note: minor is read as a noun, a young child, rather than as trivial: the problem of a baby's skin

explanation.surface: A minor skin problem, as a doctor might dismiss a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor' looks like 'not serious' but means an infant, whose skin suffers in the obvious place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the rash babies get from wet nappies (diapers), a skin complaint of the very young.

clue.text: See 1
Annoyed they're going up

parts.note: when someone is annoyed their neck feathers are said to rise, from the idiom about raised feathers

explanation.surface: An irritated remark that something, perhaps prices, is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to raise one's hackles' means to make one angry.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the neck feathers or hairs that bristle in anger, figuratively raised when a person is irritated.

clue.text: Doctor in US does enough for rollicking — that's characteristic

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters within the scrambled words
rollicking means boisterous and lively, so the letters romp into a new order

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An American doctor does enough for a boisterous patient, and that is typical of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rollicking' shuffles US DOES ENOUGH FOR, and 'in' places MO among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to laugh easily is a personal trait, the kind listed in lonely-hearts adverts as a characteristic.

clue.text: Dire accommodation had little impact

parts.note: fell is an old word for fierce or dreadful, as in one fell swoop
a flat is an apartment, a place to live

explanation.surface: Awful lodgings that made little impression on anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a joke or plan that fails to produce the expected effect.

clue.text: Best hot chicken pub's served — fellow tucking in

indicators.note: the fellow is tucked into the rearranged letters, as a diner tucks in
served as in dished up, so the words are put out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The pub's hot chicken is the best, and a man is tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges HOT CHICKEN PUB, and 'tucking in' puts F among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the finest of a group, the one you would choose first.

clue.text: Disallow try by a Northampton flanker — dead right!

parts.note: to ban is to disallow
a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: a flanker is on the side, so one outer letter of Northampton is taken

explanation.surface: A referee disallows a try scored by a Northampton flanker, and is absolutely right to.
explanation.walkthrough: Northampton is an English rugby club, where a flanker is a forward; 'try' looks like rugby but means GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for exactly correct, spot on.

clue.text: 'Roger Taylor is inside' (Queen fan)

indicators.note: inside places the little word within the jumbled letters
to roger is slang for having sex with, roughly treating the name that follows so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A headline that Queen's drummer Roger Taylor is in the building, cheered by a fan of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Taylor really is Queen's drummer, but 'Roger' is a verb (slang for having sex with) jumbling the surname to ROYALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the monarchy is an admirer of the King or Queen.

clue.text: See 1
Leaflet on bats ignored

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A leaflet about bats that nobody bothered to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left alone means being disregarded or not bothered by others.

clue.text: Hal's fielding position?

parts.note: a stop is a halt, and halt cut short drops its last letter to leave the clue's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks where Hal is fielding in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: shorten a synonym of 'stop' (HALT) to get HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the position between second and third base is a fielding role.

clue.text: Issue stops champs returning for final appearance

indicators.note: stops as in plugs, so the son fills the middle of the reversed word
returning means the word for champs is read backwards

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily, or gnaw
a son is issue, meaning offspring

explanation.surface: A dispute stops the champions coming back for one last show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champs' looks like winners but is the verb meaning chews; 'returning' turns it to SWANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The last performance of a career, named after the song a swan was fabled to sing before dying.

clue.text: See 7
Duo getting frisky with nuns? That's doubtful!

indicators.note: frisky means playful and lively, so the letters jump around

explanation.surface: A pair getting playful with nuns, which seems questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound reasoning is open to doubt, not well founded.

clue.text: Frequently stops with not much money raised, though it will cover accommodation

indicators.note: stops as in plugs a hole, so it sits inside the other word
in a down clue raised means read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: poor means having little money
oft is a poetic word for often

explanation.surface: Someone often stops with little cash raised, though a covering for lodgings is promised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads a word upwards, giving ROOP; 'stops' means plugging its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a roof covers the building below, the housing it protects.

clue.text: Hamper's back — starts to eat ravenously

parts.note: hind means rear, at the back

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A picnic basket is back and everyone begins to eat greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb, to impede.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to obstruct or impede progress, a synonym.

clue.text: Bid that liberal America would welcome?

definitions.meaning: in bridge, a call to play without a trump suit
a situation without Donald Trump, which liberal Americans would cheer

explanation.surface: A bid that American progressives would happily applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge call naming no trump suit, which also reads as being rid of the president.

clue.text: Nothing live on TV till The Voice

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all
L is an abbreviation for live, as on electrical wiring
a TV is a television set
to can mean till, as in from nine to five

explanation.surface: Nothing is being broadcast live until the talent show The Voice comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Voice is a TV singing contest, but the definition is just a kind of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is a high singing voice produced above the normal male range.

clue.text: Date Times girl finally accepted … for pay

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the dating word holds the other letters

parts.note: to see someone is to date them
T is an abbreviation for time, so times gives two of them

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of girl

explanation.surface: A girl's dating column in The Times is finally accepted for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two Ts; SEE holds TT and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill is to pay it.

clue.text: Material audience's influenced

indicators.note: an audience hears, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: swayed means influenced

explanation.surface: The material an audience took in was persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is soft napped leather, a material for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Felicity's content, not being banned

indicators.note: content as in contents, the letters inside the name

explanation.surface: Felicity is happy with something that is not prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means what is inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or permitted, the opposite of forbidden.

clue.text: Gripped by desire, regularly touch stripper

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of touch

explanation.surface: Someone overcome with desire keeps touching an exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripper' suggests a dancer, but a locust swarm strips fields bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts swarm and strip crops of their leaves, so one is a stripper of vegetation.

clue.text: See 9
Switch expected following long-standing enmity

indicators.note: switch means turn round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: A change that was anticipated after years of bad blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a prolonged quarrel between families or groups, bitter hostility.

clue.text: Table-topper's manager going back to before 2nd April

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is a famous football manager

indicators.note: going back reverses the run of letters that follows

parts.note: pre means before

indicators.note: 2nd picks the second letter of April

explanation.surface: The league leader's manager looks back to before early April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table-topper' looks like a top football club (Guardiola's), but means something set on a dining table; 'going back' reverses TO PRE P to PERPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepper shaker stands on a dining table, so it tops the table.
